title: Guardrails (2): emergency fund, STP, cooling-off, pre-commitment
objectives: Set up the emergency fund, STP and cooling-off rule at onboarding.
Run the pre-commitment conversation in writing.
body_md:
Emergency fund kept separately: short-term needs never force equity sales — counters panic selling. STP for large sums: lump sums enter equity over 6–12 months — counters regret aversion. “Cooling-off” rule: no switch or redemption decided on the same day as a big market move — counters panic and FOMO.

| Guardrail | How it works | Bias it counters |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Emergency fund kept separately | Short-term needs never force equity sales | Panic selling |
| STP for large sums | Lump sums enter equity over 6–12 months | Regret aversion |
| "Cooling-off" rule | No switch or redemption decided on the same day as a big market move | Panic, FOMO |

The pre-commitment conversation: at onboarding, agree in writing what the client will do if markets fall 20%, and what they will not do. Clients are far more likely to stay the course when they are reminded of a decision they made themselves.

> **Investor takeaway:** Decide your rules in calm times and follow them in volatile times.
example: Client agrees in writing: “If markets fall 20%, I will keep SIPs running and call you before selling.” In the fall, that sentence does the work.
say: No switch or redemption decided on the same day as a big market move.
Clients stay the course when reminded of a decision they made themselves.
never: Decide switches on the day of a big market move.

check.q: Which guardrail best counters regret aversion when investing a large lump sum?
check.why: An STP over 6–12 months. Staggering entry means no single day decides the outcome.

check.q: What does the cooling-off rule say?
o: No switch or redemption on the same day as a big market move
check.why: Cooling-off rule: no switch or redemption decided on the same day as a big market move.

check.why: STP for large sums: lump sums enter equity over 6–12 months. Counters regret aversion.
